lockup.summary: Directors, officers and holders of 5% or more of the shares agreed not to sell for 180 days after the offering closes, with limited exceptions.

what: A Singapore company licensed to move money across borders, offering payment collection, payment on behalf of clients, and brokerage services.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about US$17,872,982 and plans to spend 35% on new markets, 30% on an AI risk and compliance platform, 20% on payment settlement systems, and 15% on general business needs.
risks: Its growth depends on keeping and attracting customers, and two main customers make up most of its processed volume and can leave at any time.
It has had both losses and profits in recent periods and may lose money in the future.
A few customers bring in most of its revenue, so losing one could seriously hurt its results.
If it fails to follow rules against money laundering and terrorism financing, its business could suffer.
Its new AI risk tools may not work as expected, which could harm its compliance, operations and reputation.
